sections.title: Level 2 Strategy
sections.content: In Level 2, identifying the subject can be slightly difficult because phrases may appear between the subject and the verb. Step 1: Identify the main subject of the sentence. Step 2: Check whether there is a joining phrase in the middle (such as 'as well as', 'along with', etc.). Step 3: Identify whether the noun is countable or uncountable. Step 4: Choose the correct verb according to the subject.

sections.title: 'As well as', 'Along with', 'Together with', 'Besides'
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the main subject at the beginning of the sentence. Step 2: Check whether the sentence contains phrases like 'as well as', 'along with', 'together with', or 'besides'. Step 3: Remember that the verb always agrees with the first subject. Example: 'Ram along with his friends is coming.' Here the verb agrees with 'Ram'.

sections.title: 'A number of' vs 'The number of'
sections.content: Step 1: Identify whether the phrase is 'a number of' or 'the number of'. Step 2: 'A number of' means many, so it takes a plural verb. Step 3: 'The number of' refers to the total count, so it takes a singular verb. Example: 'A number of students are absent.' But 'The number of students is increasing.'

sections.title: Fractions and Percentages
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the fraction or percentage (one-third, half, 20%, etc.). Step 2: Check whether the noun after 'of' is countable or uncountable. Step 3: If it is uncountable, use a singular verb; if it is a plural countable noun, use a plural verb. Example: 'One-third of the milk is finished.' But 'One-third of the students are absent.'

sections.title: Indefinite Pronouns (Some, All, None, Most)
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the indefinite pronoun (some, all, none, most). Step 2: Check the noun after 'of'. Step 3: Choose the verb according to whether the noun is countable plural or uncountable. Example: 'Some of the water is dirty.' But 'Some of the students are late.'

sections.title: 'Not only... but also'
sections.content: Step 1: Identify both subjects. Step 2: Check which subject is closest to the verb. Step 3: The verb agrees with the nearest subject. Step 4: Maintain a balanced structure. Example: 'Not only the teacher but also the students are present.'

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 2 questions, a phrase often appears in the middle and hides the real subject. In sentences with 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject. 'A number of' takes a plural verb while 'The number of' takes a singular verb. In fractions, percentages, and indefinite pronouns, the verb changes according to the type of noun that follows.

tricks.title: Ignore the Middle Phrase
tricks.explanation: Temporarily remove phrases like 'as well as' or 'along with' and focus on the main subject.
tricks.example: Ram along with his friends is coming.

tricks.title: 'A number of' = Many
tricks.explanation: 'A number of' means many, so it takes a plural verb.
tricks.example: A number of players are injured.

tricks.title: 'The number of' = Total
tricks.explanation: 'The number of' refers to the total count, so it takes a singular verb.
tricks.example: The number of players is increasing.

tricks.title: Fraction Rule
tricks.explanation: After a fraction, check the noun. If it is uncountable, use a singular verb.
tricks.example: Half of the milk is wasted.

tricks.title: Fraction with Plural Noun
tricks.explanation: If the noun is plural countable, use a plural verb.
tricks.example: Half of the students are absent.

tricks.title: Indefinite Pronoun Check
tricks.explanation: For 'some', 'all', 'none', 'most', the verb depends on the noun that follows.
tricks.example: Most of the work is done.

tricks.title: Plural Noun After Indefinite
tricks.explanation: If the noun is plural, the verb will also be plural.
tricks.example: Most of the students are ready.

tricks.title: Not Only Structure
tricks.explanation: In 'not only... but also', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it.
tricks.example: Not only Ram but also his friends are coming.
